form.label: Scoring model
form.description: How evidence is weighted and how the 0-100 follow-up score is produced. Tune thresholds with command options or local/es_finding_evidence.conf.

div.p: Each finding gets a score from 0 to 100. The score answers: should an analyst follow up?

ul.li: 0–29 No — likely false/benign; do not open an investigation.
30–49 Review — glance at the evidence and the recommended searches.
50–100 Yes — investigation required. Higher scores should be handled first.

div.p: Score = 22% urgency + 18% risk + 22% observed evidence + 18% triage disposition + 10% kill-chain phase + 10% corroboration.

Observed evidence starts at 50 (neutral) and moves up or down as supporting or refuting items are attached. Unrun recommended searches never inflate the live score; they only raise the ceiling shown on the workbench.

ES 8.6 Triage agent fields (summary, justification, tools, evidence, analysis details, recommended disposition) are parsed from finding fields or notes. True-positive recommendations raise the score; high-confidence false/benign recommendations lower it and can force a No decision unless urgency is critical.

search.query: | loadfindings mode=demo | stats count by investigation_required
| loadfindings mode=demo | eval triage_disposition=if(triage_present=0,"not_run",triage_disposition) | chart median(followup_score) as median_score by triage_disposition
| loadfindings mode=demo | sort - followup_score | table followup_score, investigation_required, finding_id, title, urgency, risk_score, triage_disposition, evidence_net_weight, score_breakdown_json
